name: toy-workshop
summary: A tiny person-scale world inside a giant machine: teal plaster walls, worn blue-teal tiles, oversized screws and nuts, warm caged lamps against cool fill, X-ray glass cutaways that glow electric blue.

plaster.note: mottled: two palette blues blended with low-frequency noise, darker lower band at ~1/3 height

tile.note: square tiles, dark grout, each tile's tint jittered ±6%, scuffs only from greyscale maps

metal.note: brushed steel and brass on the giant hardware; roughness map only

painted_metal.note: machine_red and oxblood bases with chipped edges

xray.note: housing turns to glass with glowing edge lines; the part inside stays solid; add spark arcs in 'spark'

glow_ring.note: for numbers and gauges: an emissive ring that fills, lit from inside

lighting.mood: cool teal fill from above, one warm practical lamp in shot, a green-yellow wash spilling across the wall

practical.note: a caged bulb on the wall; it should be visible in the wide shot

wash.note: large soft area light, upper left, grazing the wall

lighting.accent_shots: for the twist or number beat, drop the room and light it with violet/magenta glow against 'night'

angles: high angle looking down into the room (most shots)
low angle looking up for the twist beat
camera.scale_rule: the character is ~1/6 of frame height in wides; hardware props are 2-4x the character
rules: one shot every 1.5-2.5 s, hard cuts between shots
slow push or drift in every hold; whip-blur only into the twist shot
deep focus on wides, shallow only on close-ups
every move starts on the word that names it

character.name: Tack
character.design: an original palm-sized clockwork worker: round copper body, orange enamel helmet with one headlamp, stubby jointed limbs, a brass wind-up key on the back
character.job: the viewer's stand-in who reacts to each beat (turns, points, jumps back)
character.note: designed for this channel; not based on any character in the references

story: character in the miniature room in the first second
cut to the giant part that matters
X-ray the machine to show the hidden mechanism
something goes wrong (sparks, belt snaps, light dies)
loop back to the opening room

captions.note: references show no captions on screen; using the channel's default preset

overlays.numbers: white bold inside a glowing violet ring, set in the upper half
overlays.safe_zone: nothing in the bottom 20% except captions; keep clear of the right 120 px

palette: small wind-up ratchet for the character

source: Feel measured from three user-supplied reference frames (refs/shot_4.png, shot_13.png, shot_22.png). Palette, light, lens and composition only; no characters, logos, artwork or wording taken.
